summary: Dead duplicate generators, each with a test that tests the dead copy
detail: codegen/pinia.ts (generatePiniaStore) is never used: the CLI uses subscribable_store.ts. codegen/realtime.ts (generateAffectedKeysFunction) is never used: the compiler uses the one in subscribable_sql.ts. tests/pinia.test.ts and tests/realtime.test.ts test the dead copies, a false green. Remove both modules; move any assertion worth keeping onto the live generators.
stripReferences, formatValidationResults and validatePath are defined and never called. compilePermission's context argument is unused at every call site.

summary: A build artifact and old notes are committed
detail: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo changes on every tsc run; untrack it and add it to .gitignore. docs/feature-requests/ is closed bug reports and a stale gap list; docs/futures.md is ideas, now items in this file. Remove both.

summary: Temporal entities get parallel copies of save and delete
detail: generateTemporalSaveFunction and generateTemporalDeleteFunction repeat most of the normal generators, so every fix has to be made twice (the October permission fixes were). Fold them into one generator with temporal branches; the temporal integration tests are the safety net. Keep the feature.

summary: Affected keys are found by guessing foreign-key names
detail: generateAffectedKeysFunction derives FK columns from relation names (rel + _id) and a singularize that strips a trailing s. Use the includes' declared filters and the schema's REFERENCES instead, and fail the build when a relation can't be resolved.

summary: Whether a rule reads JSONB or a row is decided by the variable's name
detail: toSource treats any name starting p_ or v_ as JSONB. Callers should pass a RowSource explicitly; most already can.
Check what of it is used and shrink it to that.

summary: Generated functions are SECURITY DEFINER, so the generated predicate is the only guard
detail: Any compiler bug in a permission check is a data leak, as October showed. The handover's direction for delta: run compiled functions as the invoker under FORCE RLS so row-level security is the backstop. Decide whether dzql adopts that or the path compiler moves to delta.

summary: Included rows in a subscription are not filtered by their own entities' view rules
detail: A document shows every included row of a root the subscriber may see. Documented in for_ai.md; decide whether includes should apply their own view rules.

summary: Large documents are built as one JSON value
detail: From docs/futures.md: a subscribable document is assembled in memory as one jsonb. Measure with large lists; consider streaming or paging.

summary: Notifications are computed inside the write transaction
detail: From docs/futures.md: affected keys and notify users are computed per write. Consider decoupling, logical replication (WAL) instead of LISTEN/NOTIFY, and a prepared statement cache. can_receive now adds a query per subscriber per push; measure it.

summary: The bench never measures RLS: it runs as the compose superuser, and its policy breaks for a real app role
detail: the test compose makes its user the bootstrap superuser, so every adapter in bench/run.ts (and the published results-0.3.0.md) ran with the policy bypassed. Run as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, the bench policy throws 22P02: after a transaction-local set_config commits, a pooled connection reads app.user_id as '' not NULL, and ''::int fails; rls.md prescribes NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::int. Fix: (1) NULLIF in bench/schema.ts; (2) run the adapters as an app role (two pools as rls.md: admin for applyFramework, schema and seed; app role with USAGE/DML and EXECUTE for writeOp), by BENCH_APP_PG_URL or SET ROLE; (3) refuse to run when rolsuper or rolbypassrls; (4) correct bench/README.md and relabel or re-run results-0.3.0.md. Measured (PG 16, loopback): RLS adds ~5 us to a static UPDATE but ~490 us (~20%) to a delta_apply_as write, the generic engine re-planning the policy in its dynamic queries. Acceptance: bun run bench passes as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, refuses a superuser or BYPASSRLS role, and the README and results say what is measured. Note 2026-10-15: Postgres is moving to dzql (compiled); this bench, and the 20% it found, go with it.
note: 2026-10-15: moved from delta's todo #77 with the bench, when delta dropped Postgres (plan step 4). The ~20% the bench found is the framework SQL's; compiled SQL (2c) is measured against it once the bench runs as an app role. | 2026-10-15: fixed -- NULLIF in the policy, every timed write as bench_app (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS), a refusal to run as a role that bypasses RLS, README and results relabelled; measured framework vs compiled (bench/results-2026-10-15.md).

summary: At the end of 2c the framework SQL retires: every document compiled, no _framework fallbacks or dispatchers
detail: Decided 15 October (Workshop docs/postgres-split-plan.md, 2c). Once the last delta_apply slice and the ledger walk are compiled, one change removes 001a-001g's interpreting functions, the dispatchers and the _framework names; what reads no definitions stays (the _delta_* tables, versions, ops log, ledger storage, serials, _delta_held). Documents registered by hand (test fixtures) move to defineDoc and generateSql; a hand-written DocType is unaffected. tests/compile's equivalence tests retire with the framework: each piece is then proven by delta's cases and its pinned text. Breaking: an app re-applies generateSql once. Removes the rule that generateSql follows applyFramework.
note: 2026-10-15: decided by Peter; ledgered while 2c slice 2 (the root check) is under way.

summary: What a write still builds from text after 2c slice 4: an add's INSERT, cascades, hanging rows, an implied root's first write
detail: _delta_insert_sql names the columns the row gives (one it leaves out takes its database default, as SQLite's insertRow), so its column list is the row's: compile it as a statement per set of keys, or keep it dynamic and say so. _delta_cascade_rows / _delta_cascade_remove and _delta_hanging_rows walk _delta_collections at run time; the implied root's existence and read in delta_apply's head are EXECUTEs. Each is a slice before the framework retires (todo #26).
note: 2026-10-15: found while compiling the row SQL (slice 4); the slice left these as they were.
